items.title: Postmortem: PricingSvc stale prices (2026-08-14)
items.text:
Postmortem: PricingSvc stale prices (2026-08-14)
Author: Leo Martinez, Senior Engineer, Technology
Incident: INC-2026-0814-01 (SEV1)
Status: Final draft for review. This is a blameless postmortem. The goal is to fix systems and processes, not to assign fault.

Summary
From 09:31 ET to roughly 16:55 ET on Friday 2026-08-14, PricingSvc kept serving the last good prices it had received instead of current ones. The root cause was an expired vendor TLS certificate on the MarketDataFeed connection to our primary pricing vendor.

PricingSvc did not fail outright. It served stale cached prices with no error and no staleness signal. That is why the problem ran for more than four hours before anyone declared an incident.

Timeline (all times ET, 2026-08-14 unless noted)
09:31  The vendor certificate expires and the TLS handshake from the MarketDataFeed handler starts failing. The handler retries with backoff and logs at WARN only. No alert fires.
09:31 onward  PricingSvc keeps serving its last cached marks. Its health checks stay green because the service itself is up.
~11:30  Traders informally notice that some intraday marks are not moving. This is treated as a quiet tape.
13:40  OMS pre-trade price checks start rejecting a growing share of orders, because limit prices fall outside the tolerance band around the stale reference price.
13:47  I declare a SEV1 in #incidents.
13:52  The incident record is opened.
13:55  Daniel Reyes confirms OMS rejections and that TradeBlotter P&L is frozen.
14:03  Owen Gallagher reports that RiskEngine VaR is stale and intraday limit monitoring is not possible.
14:20  Ravi Patel flags the risk to SettlementEngine and to the overnight ReconLegacy run if prices are not backfilled.
15:38  Omar Brown finds the handshake failures in the MarketDataFeed handler logs and confirms that the certificate expired at 09:31.
16:50  The vendor issues a renewed certificate and Barbara Beard deploys it to the feed handler.
16:55  Live ticks resume and PricingSvc marks begin updating.
17:15  Incident resolved. Backfill of 09:31 to 16:55 prices begins.
2026-08-15 morning  The backfill completes. SettlementEngine's cycle runs late, and ReconLegacy produces breaks that Operations clears manually.

Root Cause
The primary vendor rotated its certificate chain, and the client-side certificate we present had a fixed expiry. The certificate was installed by hand in 2025. It was not in any inventory or renewal calendar, so nobody owned its renewal.

Three contributing factors turned a short outage into a long silent one:
1. The feed handler treats handshake failures as retryable and does not escalate.
2. PricingSvc has no staleness threshold on cached prices.
3. Downstream systems cannot tell a stale price from a fresh one.

Impact
Direct consumers of PricingSvc:
RiskEngine: VaR and exposure figures were stale all afternoon, so Risk could not monitor limits.
OMS: orders were rejected on price checks from about 13:40 until recovery. The desk worked a small number of orders manually by phone with the executing brokers.
TradeBlotter: P&L was frozen.
PortfolioMgr: Wealth Management halted scheduled rebalancing.

Second-order effects:
SettlementEngine: delayed the next morning, because it depends on OMS trade data that was late and incomplete.
ReportingBI: dashboards fed by RiskEngine showed stale exposure until the backfill finished.
ReconLegacy: the end-of-day batch depends on SettlementEngine and GLCore, so it generated breaks. Tasha Greene and the recon team cleared them by mid-morning Saturday.

No client-facing pricing errors have been identified. No regulatory reporting deadline was missed.

What Went Well
Once the incident was declared, every affected team flagged its impact within 35 minutes. The vendor turned around the certificate renewal quickly. The backfill tooling worked on the first run.

What Went Poorly
It took more than four hours to detect the problem. Health checks measured whether the service was up, not whether its data was fresh. Ownership of the certificate was unclear.

Action Items
AI-1  Add price staleness alarms to PricingSvc. Page if more than 2% of active instruments have not ticked in 5 minutes during market hours. Owner: Leo Martinez. Due 2026-08-28.
AI-2  Put every vendor and client TLS certificate into central inventory with 30, 14, and 3-day expiry alerts. Owner: Omar Brown. Due 2026-09-04.
AI-3  Escalate repeated MarketDataFeed handshake failures to a page after 3 consecutive failures. Owner: Barbara Beard. Due 2026-08-28.
AI-4  Onboard a secondary market data vendor with automatic failover in MarketDataFeed. Owner: Sam Okafor, with Daniel Reyes for vendor selection. Target Q4 2026.
AI-5  Add graceful degradation in OMS. Flag stale reference prices on the order ticket and allow supervised override instead of hard rejection. Owner: Kevin Zhao with the Trading desk. Due 2026-09-30.
AI-6  Expose a price-age field in PricingSvc responses so RiskEngine and PortfolioMgr can mark outputs as stale. Owner: Angelica Schneider. Due 2026-09-18.
AI-7  Document PricingSvc consumers and failover behavior. Owner: Leo Martinez. Due 2026-09-02.

items.title: PricingSvc architecture and consumers
items.text:
PricingSvc architecture and consumers
Author: Leo Martinez, Senior Engineer, Technology
Last updated: 2026-09-02
This document closes action item AI-7 from the 2026-08-14 stale prices postmortem.

Purpose
PricingSvc is the firm's single source of instrument prices and valuations for intraday use. It is a critical-tier service owned by Technology. This document covers its upstream dependency, its consumers, its SLAs, its caching behavior, and what happens when it degrades.

Upstream
PricingSvc has one upstream dependency: MarketDataFeed. MarketDataFeed ingests real-time exchange and vendor data and normalizes it into a common tick format.

PricingSvc subscribes to that tick stream. It then:
derives marks (last, mid, and evaluated prices for less liquid instruments);
applies the end-of-day close policy;
publishes prices over a streaming API and a request/response API.

Today MarketDataFeed connects to one primary vendor. A secondary vendor is in procurement under AI-4, with Sam Okafor and Daniel Reyes leading selection.

Direct Consumers
RiskEngine (Risk): pulls marks to compute intraday VaR and exposure. RiskEngine also depends on PositionStore for holdings.
OMS (Trading): runs pre-trade price-band checks against the PricingSvc reference price. OMS also depends on AuthSSO.
TradeBlotter (Trading): shows trader P&L. It reads prices directly from PricingSvc and order and fill data from OMS.
PortfolioMgr (Wealth Management): runs valuation and rebalancing using PricingSvc marks together with PositionStore holdings.

Indirect Consumers
These systems never call PricingSvc, but they inherit its failures:
SettlementEngine depends on OMS, and through it on trade flow.
ReportingBI depends on RiskEngine, along with GLCore and DataLake.
ReconLegacy depends on SettlementEngine and GLCore. On 2026-08-14 the breaks reached ReconLegacy through this path, not through any pricing call.

When planning maintenance or reviewing an incident, treat all of these systems as being in scope.

SLAs
Availability: 99.95% during market hours, 07:00 to 18:00 ET, Monday to Friday.
Latency: p99 under 50 ms for request/response calls. Streaming updates must arrive within 250 ms of the MarketDataFeed tick.
Freshness (new since the incident): during market hours, no more than 2% of active listed instruments may be more than 5 minutes old. A breach pages the on-call engineer. The alarm went live on 2026-08-27.
End-of-day closing marks: published by 17:30 ET for downstream batch jobs.

Caching
PricingSvc keeps a sharded in-memory cache of last-known prices for each instrument, with a warm replica in the secondary data center.

Before the incident, cached prices never expired and responses did not carry their age. Since AI-6 shipped, every response includes price_age_ms and a stale flag. The flag is set when an instrument's price age exceeds its asset-class threshold: 5 minutes for listed equities, longer for evaluated fixed income.

Consumers are expected to act on the flag:
RiskEngine labels VaR output as stale-input.
PortfolioMgr blocks automated rebalancing.
OMS behavior is described under Failover and Degradation.

Failover and Degradation
Service failover: PricingSvc runs active-active across two data centers behind the internal load balancer. Losing one node or one site is transparent to consumers.

Data failover: this is the weak point today. If the vendor feed stops, both sites serve the same stale cache. Until the secondary vendor is live, the mitigations are:
the freshness alarm;
MarketDataFeed paging after 3 consecutive handshake failures;
expiry alerts for every vendor certificate, now tracked in the certificate inventory Omar Brown maintains.

OMS degradation: Kevin Zhao is building graceful degradation, due 2026-09-30. When a reference price is flagged stale, OMS will show a warning on the order ticket and let a desk supervisor override the price check, instead of hard-rejecting the order.

Contacts
PricingSvc on-call: Technology SRE rotation.
Service owner: Leo Martinez.
Escalation: Sam Okafor.

For anything that touches a direct consumer, notify #it-ops and the owning team's channel before making changes.
